A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite changes to the title and method name. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable, including v1's Appendices A–C. v2 contains no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 603 model–dataset cases and 34,953 production chunks, plus alert-detection, sample-size, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on 959 model–dataset cases and 36,557 production chunks, together with a sample-size experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains density-ratio estimation, weighted calibration on reference data, and expected-metric computation on production predictions. M-CBPE is renamed PAPE. Correcting the mislabeled production input in step 1a and revising the explanation do not establish a substantive procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five Folktables prediction tasks across all 50 states and 2015–2018. v2 removes the downstream significant-performance-change detection scenario evaluated in v1 Section 4.2. Additional monitored model types change configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator set is retained, with CONSTANT renamed TEST SET. However, RT-mod changes from adding a reference-fitted constant offset in v1 to applying a linear-regression correction in v2. ATC, DoC, CBPE, and IW remain evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds deep learning and XGBoost monitored models and a filter excluding cases with reference AUROC below 0.5, changing the evaluation cohort. It removes relative-error and alert-classification evaluation metrics. The sample-size study contracts from three monitored models, three metrics, and sizes up to 20,000 to LGBM/AUROC and sizes up to 5,000; the main temporal split and 2,000-observation chunks remain.

E4.justification: v2 removes the alert-threshold sweep, Appendix B's performance-versus-variability analysis, and Appendix C's estimated-versus-realized diagnostics. It substantially narrows sample-size sensitivity testing. The rolling analysis by performance-change magnitude is retained, and a short model-wise PAPE-versus-IW finding is added.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.4 newly reports paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests against the second-best method, with p = 0.0. Both versions use 500 resamples to estimate standard errors; v2 explicitly specifies sampling with replacement. No increase in repeated experiment runs is documented.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 1 with revised aggregates: proposed-method MASTE for accuracy/AUROC/F1 changes from 0.97/0.98/0.89 to 0.99/1.00/0.91. These use different cohorts, not comparable settings demonstrating deterioration. Relative-error, alert-detection, and appendix results disappear, while sample-size results are replaced under narrower settings. v2's prose retains the old baseline F1 MASTE of 2.49 although its table reports 2.54.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 adds a self-contained lemma, proof, and calibration-error decomposition, conditioning calibration on original classifier scores rather than calibrated outputs. It removes v1's Bayes-rule density-ratio derivation and Appendix A's mathematical constructions for confusion-matrix metrics and AUROC. This substantially revises the formal treatment without establishing a method change.

C1.justification: The central contributions of label-free performance estimation under covariate shift and an evaluation framework remain. v2 drops v1's explicit regression-extension claim and specific superiority claims for alert classification and small samples. It also presents PAPE without the earlier qualification that the method refines CBPE.

C2.justification: The concept-shift, support-overlap, and finite-data limitations remain. v2 develops the discussion of calibration uncertainty and proposes future cross-validated Beta-based estimation intervals instead of improved density ratios and conformal coverage. It removes v1's sparse-bucket caution and Appendix C's interpretation that conservative small-change estimates are desirable.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports the i7-11800H hardware, runtime exceeding 120 hours, and a 1,000-observation stride for the sample-size study. The cited code repository changes from NannyML/paper_mcbpe to pape-research/pape_r. Conversely, v1's DoC settings of 2,000 observations and 200 resampling repetitions are no longer specified; this is lost documentation, not evidence those settings changed.

R1.justification: v1 explicitly positions M-CBPE as an extension of earlier CBPE and credits Roth's notes for its foundations. v2 removes those citations and provenance discussion, presenting CBPE as a simpler version of PAPE. Foundational citations also shift from Roth and Sugiyama to Kim and Murphy, substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative, creates a separate Related work section, combines experimental methodology and results, and nests the sample-size study within evaluation. It also renames the paper and method, adds Albert Bifet to the byline, and removes the appendices and funding disclosure.

P2.justification: v2 removes the relative-error and alert-results tables and the alert and appendix figures. The two multi-panel sample-size figures are replaced by one AUROC panel, and CBPE receives a pseudocode display. Figures 1 and 2 reuse the original graphics with revised placement and captions, but still contain the old M-CBPE and CONSTANT terminology.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens monitored-model testing, provides a more self-contained theoretical argument, and adds significance testing. However, it removes the alert evaluation, diagnostic appendices, and explanation of applying the estimator to non-additive metrics while retaining the any-metric claim. Outdated figure legends and a new table–text numerical inconsistency further weaken clarity. These substantive gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
